nodes.original_target: Dynamics on the lift are reversible linear isometries. QM_122 H003 shows deterministic report dynamics do not by themselves give reversibility; H006 gives a permutation isometry envelope that is not a Hilbert unitary.

Probability is additive over orthogonal sectors and defined on projections / frames. This couples the l1 additivity of sectors to Hilbert-space orthogonality. Under frame additivity the quartic rival dies (H013FrameAdditivity), and without it two effect rules share the unit total and disagree (H013SameContract).

The lift c_i = sqrt(w_i) e^{i theta_i} needs a coefficient field with square roots of the weights. Over Q this fails in general; Rust exact_amplitudes returns None unless each normalized weight is a rational square.

U(1) phases (unit complex numbers) act on sector amplitudes. QM_122 shows a sign carrier suffices for some finite tasks and that excluding it needs an extra non-exponent-two condition. The selector for C / U(1) belongs to QM_028 / QM_062 (another segment).

For integer lists v the diagonal trace norm equals sum |v_i| (trace_norm_eq_mass). Scaling by c != 0 keeps the normalized absolute weights and, for |c|>1, raises the mass. Reconstruction without an admitted mass returns failure. The real operator embedding is not constructed in Lean. C05: the trace embedding carries no physical state or quantum claim.

Diagonal Markov-composable channels factor through the residual density carrier (qm003_c17_diagonal_composable_factorization), while Hadamard off-diagonal coherence separates matrix composition from diagonal multiplication.
Branch-localization and many-worlds readings of the lifted phases are conjectures, not part of the QM_020 theorems.

For weights w with total W != 0, P = w/W sums to one, is idempotent under renormalization, and P(w) = P(w') iff w, w' lie on the same positive ray. Lean (BornRedundancy.lean) states this over List Rat.
For disjoint supports the l1 additivity defect is zero iff the entries have the same sign (D1). The strict l^p subadditivity for p>1 is stated for natural exponents in the finite kernel only.
Strict l^p (p>1) subadditivity on disjoint supports follows from standard Minkowski / strict convexity. The paper cites it as standard analysis.
A linear map that is descent-compatible (respects the l1 weight descent on a chosen sector basis, with phase rotation freedom) is monomial, i.e. strictly row-sparse. Lean covers the 2x2 real case.

Given a supplied lift c with |c_i|^2 = w_i (for example c_i = sqrt(w_i) e^{i theta_i}), |c_i|^2 / sum |c|^2 = w_i / sum w. So the Born-form probability of the lift equals the l1 normalization, and the lift is redundant for probability. Existence of the lift requires square roots (not available over Q in general) and a complex structure.

Under a chosen Hilbert lift with independent Haar-uniform phases, E |<u, psi(theta)>|^2 = sum |u_gamma|^2 w_gamma. Worked replay w=(2,1,1) gives 37/16. Rust replaces Haar by a declared finite phase group (decided for n <= 3). The paper says it must not be upgraded without full Hilbert and Haar discharge.
Additive sector weights alone do not force the quadratic Born form: other normalized maps from the same weights give the same additive structure. This is a scope statement.

Born-quadratic uniqueness holds only under imported assumptions: finite additive weights, complex linear Hilbert representation, phase-blind positive descent map, orthogonal additivity, reversible lifted dynamics by linear isometries, interference as bilinear cross terms, projection-measure / frame-function structure. For dim >= 3 Gleason gives Tr(rho Pi); dim 2 needs a POVM variant. This is the Born-uniqueness firewall.

The Hilbert lift is probability-redundant (Thm 4) but dynamics-capable: it can host interference and reversible linear dynamics that l1 weights alone cannot. This is a capacity statement about the representation, not a derivation that physical dynamics are linear or unitary.

Ladder over QM_020 rung 1: diagonal density (2), channels as stochastic kernels (3), path-sum as matrix power (4), superposition phase content as quotient fiber U(1)^(|E_w|-1) (5), interference as non-l1 cross term (6). The ceiling of the ladder is the C/U(1) carrier, Born-quadratic uniqueness (Gleason) and the continuum / unitarity limit, all imported.

A pairing exists (pairing_exists), a quartic rival to the quadratic pairing exists (quartic_rival), and uniqueness is not discharged (uniqueness_not_discharged, born_nonuniqueness_open). Under frame additivity the fourth power is excluded. Ordinary Gleason dimension is not matched by the two-label host (H017Gleason).

A sign carrier ({+1,-1}) suffices for the finite phase tasks tested (sign_carrier_suffices) and the circle is not forced: excluding the sign group needs an extra condition, and the circle itself stays imported.

The finite Hilbert boundary from primitive difference does not recover ordinary M_n(C). Open: Gleason at n >= 3, CPTP, tensor uniqueness, circle, Python dual. Imports listed in section 7: complex scalars as a field, circle phases, Born uniqueness (Gleason), Hilbert tensor, CPTP, continuous time. H017Finish gives a declared finish table, not a derivation.
